references.text: Jesus refers to the woman as a daughter of Abraham whom Satan had bound for eighteen years and who needed to be released from her bonds – a direct explanation of the healing in verse 12, where he declares her free from her sickness. [ref:Luk 13:16|Luke 13:16]

Jesus quotes Isaiah and proclaims his mission: to preach freedom for captives and give sight to the blind – his declaration to the woman in 13:12 that she is released from her sickness fulfills this program. [ref:Luk 4:18|Luke 4:18]

Isaiah prophesies about the anointed one who will preach freedom for captives and open prison for the bound – Jesus releases the woman from her sickness as a fulfillment of this prophecy. [ref:Jes 61:1|Isaiah 61:1]

Jesus addresses the dead young man and commands him to rise – a similar pattern where Jesus takes the initiative, speaks to the suffering one, and grants healing or resurrection by his word, just as he does toward the woman in 13:12. [ref:Luk 7:14|Luke 7:14]
Jesus addresses the unclean spirit and commands it to come out – an example of Jesus authoritatively declaring people free from evil and sickness by his word. [ref:Mark 1:25|Mark 1:25]
"If the Son sets you free, you will be truly free" – Jesus' statement about liberation points to the same authority he exercises when he releases the woman from her sickness. [ref:Joh 8:36|John 8:36]

The preceding verses describe the woman who had a spirit of weakness and had been bent double for eighteen years – the immediate context for Jesus' declaration of healing in verse 12. [ref:Luk 13:11|Luke 13:11]

Jesus laid his hands on her, and immediately she straightened up and praised God – the immediate continuation showing that Jesus' words in verse 12 were followed by action and complete healing. [ref:Luk 13:13|Luke 13:13]
Peter describes Jesus' work: "he went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil" – the woman's healing in Luke 13:12 is a concrete example of this. [ref:Apg 10:38|Acts 10:38]
